newsitem.title: USA: Rivlin says room for banker on Fed board.
newsitem.headline: Rivlin says room for banker on Fed board.

text.p: Federal Reserve Vice Chair Alice Rivlin said there was room for someone with banking experience on the Fed's board.
"At the moment we don't have a banker," Rivlin told Reuters Financial Television when asked about the ideal qualities for the job.
She said a good understanding of the economy was needed but the person didn't necessarily have to be an economist.

The Clinton administration is in the process of filling two Fed vacancies that opened up the the departure earlier this year of Janet Yellen to the White House and Lawrence Lindsey to the private sector.
"There is room for a broad range of skills on the board," Rivlin said.
"We could have someone who has been in the banking industry," she said but noted that "it is difficult to find a banker who wants to give up banking to come on the Federal Reserve Board."
